item.title: NEW: CISA Issues Urgent Warning for Critical "Java4Shell" RCE Flaw
item.description:
Headline: CISA Issues Urgent Warning for Critical "Java4Shell" RCE Flaw

Summary:
A critical remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938), dubbed "Java4Shell," has been discovered in OpenJDK's Base64 decoder, affecting versions 17.0.6+ on specific x86-64 CPUs. The flaw, rated 9.2 CVSS, allows for unauthenticated RCE and impacts major enterprise applications like Jira, Confluence, and Jenkins. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued an urgent advisory for organizations to apply patches immediately.

Severity: Critical

Categories: Vulnerability, Patch Management, Threat Intelligence

Article Type: Advisory

Meta Description: CISA issues an urgent warning for CVE-2026-114938, a critical remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK and Oracle Java dubbed "Java4Shell."

The injected code was designed to steal cryptocurrency, skim payment card data, and deploy iOS exploit kits to vulnerable Apple devices. Optimizely has since remediated the issue.

item.title: UPDATE: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures
item.description:
Headline: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures

Summary:
Google's Project Zero, an elite vulnerability research team, has announced a significant change to its disclosure policy. Effective immediately, the team is eliminating the 30-day grace period previously granted for patch adoption. Under the new "Full X" policy, technical details of a vulnerability will be made public 90 days after reporting to a vendor, regardless of whether a fix is available. The deadline will be progressively shortened to 30 days by 2028 to pressure vendors into faster patching cycles.
